papers.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
papers.abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.

papers.title: Weak null singularities for the Einstein--Vlasov system
papers.abstract: We study the formation and stability of weak null singularities for solutions to the massive and massless Einstein--Vlasov systems without symmetry assumptions. Extending previous results of Luk in the vacuum setting, we establish the existence of spacetimes arising from characteristic initial data that develop a singular null boundary while remaining extendible with a continuous metric. For both massive and massless particles, the energy-momentum tensor and Ricci curvature remain bounded and extend continuously to the singular boundary. For genuinely singular initial data, the Christoffel symbols in the original double-null coordinates fail to be locally square integrable near the boundary. We introduce new commutator vector fields that avoid both derivative loss and the most singular curvature component. Under additional curvature assumptions, we also prove Lipschitz inextendibility across the singular null boundary.

papers.title: The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
papers.abstract: We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.

papers.title: Determinant Identities and Branch Selection in the Stationary Multi-Horizon Balance Problem
papers.abstract: We study the Hennig-Neugebauer family of stationary and axisymmetric vacuum multi-horizon candidates. The regularity conditions on the symmetry axis lead to quadratic determinant relations which leave an apparent ambiguity between two sign branches. Under explicit non-degeneracy assumptions, we prove that one of these branches is impossible. This branch selection yields a system of explicit determinant equations characterizing equilibrium within the family.

papers.title: Entire boosted hypersurfaces of vanishing mean curvature in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of entire maximal hypersurfaces, asymptotic to suitable coordinate-dependent boosts in the two asymptotically flat ends of maximally extended Schwarzschild spacetime. As a corollary, this generates a foliation of maximal hypersurfaces in exterior Schwarzschild, which corresponds to a geometric choice of time function associated with any boost parameter. As a crucial step in the proof, we introduce a novel rotationally symmetric time function in maximally extended Schwarzschild, which is Cauchy and has properties of independent interest.

papers.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
papers.abstract: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $\Sigma$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.

papers.title: Exact model of a gravitational wave and electromagnetic radiation in DHOST gravity theory: wave solutions and testable effects
papers.abstract: Within an analytical non-perturbative framework based on a single exact model, the coupled dynamics of gravitational waves and high-frequency electromagnetic fields is investigated in General Relativity and DHOST gravity. Using an exact gravitational-wave spacetime in an isotropic (null) wave coordinate system, Maxwell's equations are integrated analytically. This analysis provides an exact non-perturbative confirmation from the full field equations that a gravitational wave acts as a waveguide, forming a propagation channel for electromagnetic radiation co-directional with the gravitational wave and generating an effective pure-radiation source. Applying this exact electrodynamic solution to the nonlinear field equations of DHOST class~Ia gravity reveals that the algebraic structure of the DHOST constraint equations enforces a modification of the electromagnetic-wave parameters. Based on this mechanism, an observationally testable effect of scalar frequency drift is derived, providing a direct way to discriminate between General Relativity and modified gravity theories even when their metric tensors share identical functional forms.

papers.title: Machine learning and high accuracy: Neural preconditioners for computational gravity
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) developments have empowered valuable calculations in many areas of theoretical physics. Certain topics involving moderate-to-low accuracy requirements have been particularly fortunate because many ML techniques, such as neural networks, introduce a noise floor that would be difficult to penetrate with stricter tolerances. For this reason, topics requiring high accuracy can be hesitant to pursue ML. One prominent example is gravitational wave modeling, which relies on traditional methods that accommodate the high sensitivities of detectors such as LISA. However, recent progress in applied mathematics has identified hybrid methods where fast-but-noisy ML mechanisms are inserted into otherwise traditional numerical schemes to accelerate convergence in a way that ultimately meets or exceeds the accuracy of standard methods. We develop an optimized hybrid ML method to tackle a class of challenging PDEs; specifically, we demonstrate ML implementations for gravitational waves from asymmetric-mass black hole binaries and elastic waves. These require solving sparse linear algebra systems with Helmholtz features that are especially difficult for traditional iterative methods. Our new approach is to train a graph neural network (GNN) as a significantly faster preconditioner using a novel loss function based on the true residual of the iterative algorithm. For the most difficult regions of parameter space, our neural preconditioner decreases iteration counts by 2-15x compared to traditional preconditioners. Because the GNN operates directly on the sparse matrix and needs only modest physical context, it generalizes beyond its training domain and can be adapted to new problems across physics by retraining rather than redesign. Hybrid ML methods such as this offer a new and compelling avenue to handle high accuracy and speed requirements in gravitational wave modeling and beyond.

papers.title: Carrollian quantum states and flat space holography
papers.abstract: We study free Carrollian quantum field theories from an algebraic perspective and explore their implications for flat space holography. As explicit examples, we construct the electric and magnetic Carrollian Weyl algebras obtained from Carroll limits of the relativistic scalar field and analyze their states, including vacuum and thermal configurations. For the massive electric theory, we find a regular Carroll-invariant vacuum state and a regular KMS state, yielding a consistent Carrollian thermodynamic system. By contrast, the massless electric and magnetic theories are more subtle: depending on the quantization, they admit either no regular distinguished vacuum or only nonregular Carroll-invariant ground states, while still supporting nonregular thermal states. We further analyze alternative classes of states in the massless electric theory, including spatially homogeneous quasifree pure states and Sorkin--Johnston states. Motivated by these results, we discuss consequences for flat space holography. We construct a well-defined state relevant for Carrollian holography whose Hilbert-space representation factorizes into a standard Fock sector and a nonseparable zero-mode sector, thereby highlighting the role of infrared degrees of freedom in the boundary theory.

papers.title: An algebra of proper observables at null infinity: Dirac brackets, Memory and Goldstone probes
papers.abstract: We develop a rigorous evaluation of Dirac brackets for classical observables on the phase space of radiative gravitational modes at null infinity that naturally incorporates memory effects. Considering the Ashtekar-Streubel phase space, with boundary conditions in time given by vanishing {\it news} and purely electric {\it shear}, and taking into account the infinite dimensionality of the phase space, we identify the algebra of proper observables (understood as functions on phase space that can be associated with smooth symplectic flows). We show that the action of supertranslation charges generate the correct transformations on the shear. We also show that the conventional definition of the ``Goldstone mode'' adopted in the literature cannot be associated with a proper observable, but nevertheless there exists an infinite family of proper observables, which we call {\it Goldstone probes}, that are capable of measuring the Goldstone mode. We notice that there are no Goldstone probes constructed only out of the shear {\it or} the news, providing a possible explanation for why attempts to construct a (separable) Hilbert space with different memory states have failed so far. Finally, we derive formulas for distributional Dirac brackets between local shear and news, and show that they contain non-local corrections.

papers.title: How much averaged null energy must an anisotropic bounce violate?
papers.abstract: We show that in Einstein gravity a null-complete, non-static Bianchi I universe (homogeneous, spatially flat and anisotropic) violates the averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along every complete light ray outside at most four null directions, and along all of them if its total energy density, cosmological constant included, is ever positive. Along each complete ray the averaged null energy is at most $-J_p/(8\pi G)$, with equality whenever the integral converges, where $J_p$ is the squared expansion and shear accumulated by a thin bundle of light rays. With spatial sections $\mathbb{R}^3$ the achronal ANEC therefore leaves only Minkowski space, as for flat and open Friedmann models. Under the pointwise null energy condition, every null geodesic of a non-static Bianchi I universe is incomplete. The isotropic bounce of effective loop quantum cosmology has $J_p=1.478\,\omega_B H_{\max}$ (light frequency at the bounce times largest Hubble rate), and at the same critical density the cheapest ray of a strongly anisotropic bounce pays four to five times as much. A Casimir-supported turning point on a three-torus has a deficit of the same order, but at Hubble rates well below the Planck scale its light rays circumnavigate the torus and are not achronal, so the achronal ANEC does not apply to them.

papers.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant. In four spacetime dimensions, the standard AdS-invariant boundary conditions set the rescaled magnetic field to zero for electromagnetism and the rescaled magnetic Weyl tensor to zero for Einstein gravity on the conformal boundary. We generalize these standard boundary conditions by setting arbitrary linear combinations of the electric and magnetic fields, or the corresponding Weyl tensors, to zero, and we conjecture that these exhaust the local, AdS-invariant, conservative boundary conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$. Boundary conditions with non-AdS-invariance and in different spacetime dimensions are also studied. The AdS-invariant conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$ extend to Yang-Mills theory and nonlinear gravity in a general Fefferman-Graham setting. We construct phase spaces for these general boundary conditions. The covariant phase spaces for general conditions are naturally associated with Lagrangians containing Pontryagin terms and, in gravity, a Gauss-Bonnet term. In gravity, except for the standard boundary condition, no nontrivial asymptotic symmetries exist and all conserved charges such as ADM mass vanish identically, as in a closed universe. Spacetimes with Killing fields including AdS then exhibit linearization instability in the sense of Fischer and Marsden and Moncrief. For nonstandard boundary conditions, the modified symplectic structure yields new expressions for the entropy formula of black holes.

papers.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
papers.abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.

papers.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
papers.abstract: In $\Lambda$CDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field $\phi$ through an exponential mass coupling $m_{\rm c}(\phi)\propto e^{-\beta\phi/M_{\rm Pl}}$ can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within $2\sigma$ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.

papers.title: A consistent formulation of stochastic inflation II: Reassessing its role in nonlinear cosmological perturbations
papers.abstract: We question whether the conventional formulation of stochastic inflation can provide a quantitatively reliable description of cosmological perturbations. More fundamentally, we reassess the role and motivations of the stochastic approach to study cosmological perturbations, distinct from its well-founded motivation for resumming IR secular divergences. To provide a quantitative basis for this reassessment, we extend stochastic inflation beyond the linear regime by incorporating non-Markovian effects arising from infrared-ultraviolet interactions and terms quadratic in ultraviolet fluctuations, which generate non-white noise. We derive three-point correlation functions for a spectator scalar field in de Sitter space and a slow-roll inflaton including metric perturbations, demonstrating exact agreement with in-in quantum-field-theoretic predictions for superhorizon nonlinear evolution. Our results show that both non-Markovian effects and quadratic (higher order) noise terms are essential for quantitative accuracy, implying that the conventional stochastic-inflation framework is, at best, quantitatively justified only at linear order.

papers.title: Non-Gaussian matter fluctuations from primordial magnetic fields and galaxy luminosity function
papers.abstract: Primordial magnetic fields (PMFs) represent a promising candidate for the origin of large-scale magnetic fields observed in astrophysical environments. Through the Lorentz force, PMFs generate matter density perturbations, leaving distinct imprints on the formation of cosmic structures. While previous studies have primarily characterized these imprints via the matter power spectrum --- a two-point statistic --- we demonstrate that the one-point statistics of PMF-induced density fluctuations reveal an intrinsically non-Gaussian probability distribution function (PDF), even when the PMFs themselves are statistically Gaussian. In particular, we find that the high-density tail of the PDF is enhanced by over two orders of magnitude relative to the Gaussian case. Adopting the Press-Schechter formalism, we show that this non-Gaussianity significantly boosts the abundance of rare objects, especially massive halos and those at high redshifts. We further compute the ultraviolet luminosity function of galaxies at $z=6$, $12$, and $16$, and compare our predictions with recent James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations that have reported an excess of high-redshift galaxies at $z\sim 12$ -- $16$ relative to standard $\Lambda$CDM expectations. Intriguingly, in the limiting case where the total density field inherits this PDF, our results suggest that the non-Gaussian density fluctuations sourced by PMFs can explain the bright-end ($M_\mathrm{UV}\lesssim -18$) excess at $z\gtrsim 12$, without requiring additional astrophysical enhancements to star-formation efficiency.

papers.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
papers.abstract: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

papers.title: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
papers.abstract: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $\Lambda$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $\Lambda$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $\Lambda$CDM at $2\sigma$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$\alpha$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.

papers.title: Improved constraints on axion inflation with the new code AxioGen: an efficient generator of curvature perturbations
papers.abstract: Axion inflation, in which a pseudoscalar inflaton couples to a $U(1)$ gauge field via a Chern-Simons interaction, has garnered significant interest due to its rich phenomenology. The power spectrum and bispectrum for this model are often parametrized by functions known as $f_2$ and $f_3$, respectively. Previous work computed $f_2$ and $f_3$ using an approximation for the gauge field mode functions. While these approximate solutions are fairly accurate ($\mathcal{O}(10\%)$) for large values of the model parameter $\xi$, which controls gauge field particle production, our recent work has shown them to be quite inaccurate for smaller values of $\xi$. We present new fitting functions for $f_2$ and $f_3$ that are significantly more accurate than those previously used. We use these functions to place new constraints on $\xi$ and also set lower bounds for the energy scale of the axion gauge field coupling for $\phi^{1/3}$ and $\phi^{2/3}$ inflationary potentials. Additionally, we present a new public code to efficiently generate realizations of the primordial curvature perturbation for axion inflation in the weak backreaction regime. This code enables numerical computation of higher order correlators and provides a novel path to initial conditions for large-scale structure formation.

papers.title: Shear, vorticity, and $f(R)$ theories
papers.abstract: We study how an extended spherical collapse model (ESCM), including shear, vorticity and chameleon screening, modifies the collapse threshold $\delta_c(z)$ and $\delta_c(M)$, the turnaround density $\delta_t$, the turnaround radius $R_t$ and the halo mass function in the Hu-Sawicki $f(R)$ model, and whether these quantities can distinguish $f(R)$ from General Relativity (GR). Unlike the standard spherical collapse model (SSCM), in the ESCM $\delta_c$ depends on mass, redshift and $|f_{R0}|$; we use it to compute the halo mass function with the excursion set approach. Between GR and the large-field (LF) limit of $f(R)$, $\delta_c$ differs by a few percent within the ESCM and by about 20% between GR in the ESCM and the LF limit in the SSCM; $\delta_t$ differs by about 27-29% and $R_t$ by about 6.5%. With screening, the difference between GR and screened $\delta_c$ is 2.5% for $|f_{R0}|=10^{-4}$ (F4) and vanishes for $|f_{R0}|=10^{-6}$ (F6); for $\delta_t$ it is larger than 20% (F4), about 10% (F5) and 0 (F6); for $R_t$ about 6.5% (F4), 3% (F5) and 0 (F6). Since observations exclude F4 and F6 is practically identical to GR, only F5 could discriminate, but the ~20% uncertainty on measured turnaround radii rules out $R_t$ and related quantities as tests of $f(R)$. The halo abundance predicted by $f(R)$, especially at high redshift, can instead distinguish $f(R)$ from GR.

papers.title: Minimal vacuum histories beyond $\Lambda$CDM: model comparison within VCDM
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological observations motivate alternatives to $\Lambda$CDM with evolving dark energy. We compare three such models, each introducing one additional cosmological parameter: F42, with equation of state $w(a)=w_0/\sqrt{a}$, and two smooth sign-changing effective dark-energy profiles, Ag and Qui. All models are implemented within VCDM, which determines the background and linear perturbations without introducing an additional propagating gravitational degree of freedom. We use CMB observations from SPT, Planck, and ACT, combined with DESI DR2 distance measurements, with and without the DESY5 Dovekie supernova sample. All three alternatives improve the best-fit likelihood relative to $\Lambda$CDM. When supernovae are included, the Akaike information criterion favors F42, while Ag and Qui remain nearly indistinguishable from $\Lambda$CDM on this criterion. The Bayesian evidence, however, does not establish a robust preference among the three alternatives. Our results show that improved fits to current observations can arise from physically different dark-energy histories, motivating complementary measurements of expansion and structure growth to distinguish them.

papers.title: Kinessence, phantom crossing and sign-switching dark energy
papers.abstract: We introduce Kinessence models where combining K-mouflage and quintessence leads to phantom-crossing of the dark energy equation of state and sign-switching of the dark energy density. This is realised by joining a dark scalar sector comprising K-essence kinetic terms and a quintessence potential together with a Yukawa coupling to matter. We investigate the dynamics of these models in the Jordan frame at the background and perturbative levels. We concentrate on the effective equation of state and the matter fraction for the background. The CMB spectra, the linear power spectrum and the growth of structure via $f\sigma_8$ are also analysed at the perturbative level. The quintessence potential drives the acceleration of the Universe at low redshift with an equation of state greater than -1. The Yukawa coupling to matter leads to a phantom crossing behaviour depending on its strength. The potential fifth force mediated by the scalar field is screened by the K-mouflage mechanism triggered by the K-essence kinetic terms and passes Solar System tests. This allows for relatively large Yukawa couplings to matter $\beta\sim 0.1$, large enough to lead to the crossing of the phantom divide at $z\sim 0.5$. Despite a significant scalar interaction on large scales, we find that the growth of structure is reduced compared to LCDM. The matter fraction deviates from the standard model by a few percent and the Hubble rate is larger at low redshift than at recombination whilst the CMB spectra show small deviations from LCDM. The dark energy fraction becomes negative at redshifts greater than 2. All these features should alleviate the various tensions such as the larger value of $H_0$ at small redshift, a possible reduction of growth as measured by $S_8$ and the bound on the sum of the neutrino masses. Deviations from LCDM of the CMB lensing spectrum may provide a detectable window for these models.

papers.title: Efficient Standard Siren Cosmological Inference with Posterior Reuse
papers.abstract: Standard siren cosmology depends on several modelling assumptions, including the underlying source population, galaxy catalogue, and detection selection function. Quantifying the effect of each choice typically requires a full, independent analysis. As gravitational-wave catalogs grow incrementally, much computational effort is spent re-analysing largely overlapping datasets. We apply the recently developed ASPIRE (Accelerated Sequential Posterior Inference via Reuse) sampler to the joint estimation of cosmological and population parameters with dark sirens. ASPIRE updates existing posterior samples into the posterior under a new hypothesis without restarting from the prior. It combines normalising flows with a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) scheme to produce accurate posteriors and unbiased evidence estimates. Applying ASPIRE to a number of dark siren analysis cases with GWTC-5.0, we recover posteriors consistent with nested sampling, while recording a performance improvement of between 6-28 times over the set of analyses when using an existing posterior. This enables efficient exploration of modelling choices and rapid updates as catalogs grow, without duplicating existing computational effort.

papers.title: Localization of gravitational-wave source behind galaxy clusters by gravitational-wave lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations have opened new opportunities to study massive object events like merging binary black holes. When combined with electromagnetic counterparts, accurate localization of gravitational-wave sources could allow us to identify their host galaxies and carry out follow-up studies, such as study the environment of merging black holes and determine the Hubble constant. One of the possible methods for precise localization is strong gravitational-wave lensing. Previous studies have considered strong gravitational-wave lensing with galaxy lenses. However, galaxy clusters have yet to be investigated due to the complexity of their mass structures. Here we take the list of known cluster lenses from the Hubble Frontier Fields, simulate lensing properties of gravitational waves from their reconstructions as they would be observed by the ground-based gravitational-wave detectors. When same model family is used in simulation and localization, we find that the correct lens is identified for around 90\% of the simulated events. We also show that the source positions within the cluster can be pinpointed at sub-arcsecond precision with an estimate on source redshift. When we marginalize over all possible lens models for the clusters, the lens identification and localizations remain valid as long as the correct lens model is contained in the available cluster lens models. However, most localization attempts fail at initialization if the correct cluster model is excluded. These tests establish a proof of concept of localization under idealized conditions, while more work is needed to understand the cluster lens modeling discrepancies and reconstruction bias to validate the approach further.

papers.title: The NANOGrav 15-year data set: A Limit on Continuous Spin Gravitons
papers.abstract: Continuous spin particles (CSPs) are massless particles characterized by a dimensionful spin scale, $\rho$, which, when non-zero, changes their helicity under Lorentz boosts. Since CSPs reduce to ordinary particles when $\rho \rightarrow 0$, the photon or graviton could be CSPs and only appear to behave as ordinary particles due to a small value of $\rho$. Therefore, it is important to determine what value of $\rho$ is experimentally allowed. Recent work has shown that the physical effects of CSPs scale as powers of $\rho/\omega$ when $\rho \ll \omega$, where $\omega$ is a frequency scale, making low-frequency probes particularly beneficial for highlighting these phenomena. In this paper we use pulsar timing arrays to set constraints on the spin scale of the continuous spin graviton. Pulsar timing arrays are uniquely suited for this application as they have exceptional sensitivity to low, nanohertz frequency gravitational waves, as demonstrated by their recent evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. Using standard Bayesian data analysis techniques, we find that the NANOGrav 15-year data set constrains the graviton spin scale to $\rho_\text{g} < 1.23 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{eV} $ at the 95% credible level.

papers.title: Rapidly Spinning Primordial Black Holes from Confinement
papers.abstract: Confinement can turn widely separated particles into rapidly spinning primordial black holes. A flux tube pulls a heavy quark--antiquark pair together, converting its stored energy into relativistic motion. The same mechanism is possible in the magnetic dual, where a Higgs phase confines magnetic flux into a string joining a monopole--antimonopole pair. As the particles approach, cosmological tides and string bends can deflect their motion and make them miss. These disturbances can originate during inflation or be generated later. Black-hole formation then requires rare close passages from a smooth, broad encounter distribution. The resulting natal spin density therefore rises linearly to extremality, with mean dimensionless spin two thirds. Numerical string evolutions recover this law. Pairs that miss can remain bound, radiate and later collapse into lighter, near-extremal holes, sourcing a stochastic gravitational-wave background. Although the abundance remains model dependent, confinement leaves a unique spin signature that gravitational-wave observations can test.

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.

papers.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
papers.abstract: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.

papers.title: Popcorn EMRIs: Transient Gravitational Wave Signals and Their Analysis in Schwartz Space
papers.abstract: This study investigates extreme-mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) with orbital periods exceeding the observation windows of mHz gravitational wave detectors. During their early, highly eccentric stages, these systems produce periodic gravitational wave eruptions at pericentre, separated by long quiescent periods. We define these systems as ``popcorn EMRIs''--bound, coherent binaries in a deterministic evolutionary phase. This distinguishes them from stochastic, non-coherent bursts associated with parabolic fly-bys. Using a steady-state model based on the phase-space continuity equation, we estimate the population within a Milky Way-like galaxy. Because these estimates depend on sensitive astrophysical variables like stellar relaxation and density profiles, our figures are illustrative rather than absolute. For a one-year observation baseline, we estimate a steady-state population of 200 to 2,000 popcorn EMRIs, significantly outnumbering the 10 to 88 continuously observable EMRIs. This yields an expected rate of 5 to 44 detectable eruptions per year. Despite high signal-to-noise ratios (exceeding 700 for Galactic Centre events), the low duty cycle confirms their transient nature. Standard data processing techniques, designed for continuous signals, often employ windowing that distorts eruption morphology and artificially reduces the signal-to-noise ratio. To address this, we establish a mathematical apparatus using based on standard smoothing techniques, in the theory of tempered distributions. We demonstrate that standard windowing techniques irreversibly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio of transient sources when the taper overlaps the eruption, and we utilize Schwartz space regularization to justify the direct Fourier transform as the energy-preserving estimator.

papers.title: QPEs from Warped Disk Collisions with EMRIs: Brightness-Recurrence Diagram and Gravitational-Wave Follow-up
papers.abstract: Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPEs) display correlated long/short and strong/weak patterns that remain unexplained by existing flat-disk collision models. We propose that these features arise from an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) colliding with a warped accretion disk, likely formed after a tidal disruption event. The warp modulates both recurrence time and burst energy, encoding the disk geometry -- and thus the spin of the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) -- into the X-ray light curve. We introduce the Brightness-Recurrence Diagram (BRD) to visualize this correlation, where QPE bursts trace an elliptical trajectory driven by the EMRI's apsidal precession; the tilt of this ellipse encodes whether the EMRI is prograde or retrograde relative to the SMBH spin. Applying this model to the prototypical QPE source GSN 069 successfully reproduces the observed patterns. The data are consistent with either a prograde stellar secondary or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. In the stellar-mass black hole scenario, ongoing orbital decay could render the EMRI detectable by LISA within a few decades, facilitating gravitational-wave follow-up and independent multimessenger constraints on the system.
